articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo: contact tracing reaches about 30,000 people, while authorities say more than 400,000 should be monitored. Jean Kaseya, director-general of Africa CDC, reported that fewer than 10% of estimated contacts are being identified. On average, each confirmed Ebola case requires locating roughly 60 individuals who had direct or indirect contact with the patient. More than 80% of newly confirmed cases arise among people not listed as contacts, signaling transmission beyond surveillance. With the outbreak now widespread in communities, officials warn that effective control is not achievable under current surveillance levels. About 7,000 confirmed Ebola cases have been recorded. This data underscores substantial gaps in contact tracing and ongoing challenges in outbreak containment in the DRC.
notes: Africa CDC幹部が監視体制の不備を公式に指摘しており、確認症例約7000件、接触者追跡率10%未満という深刻な状況。新規症例の80%以上が既知の接触者リスト外から発生しており、コミュニティ内での制御不能な感染拡大が示唆される。

Venomous bites demand immediate hospital care; do not attempt home remedies. Preventive measures include avoiding floodwater, wearing boots, hand hygiene, safe drinking water, proper food handling, eliminating standing water, and seeking care for worsening symptoms.

articleSummary: New synthetic antimalarial compounds overcome resistance. articleSummary: First officially confirmed severe human case of Oya virus infection in China (Guangdong, southern province) involving a 54-year-old goose farm worker. Lab tests showed leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, markedly elevated D-dimer and hepatic enzymes; broad-spectrum antibiotics were ineffective. A week later, conjunctival hemorrhages, petechiae, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and progressive liver failure developed; chest CT revealed bilateral pleural effusions and extensive ground-glass lung opacities. The patient recovered after aggressive therapy (corticosteroids, IV immunoglobulin, coagulation support) and was discharged on day 19, with full recovery by day 31. Metagenomic sequencing on day 8 detected Oya virus RNA in plasma; serology showed IgM/IgG. Genomic analysis (isolate GZ8H2016) matched strains from local hematophagous midges in Guangdong. In vitro and in vivo models demonstrated robust replication and phenotype consistent with human disease. Authors urge Asia-wide screening for unexplained fevers with liver/GI involvement and strengthened vector surveillance; previously, Oya was considered benign, detected in pigs and bloodsucking insects in Malaysia, China, Vietnam, and India. The report appears in The New England Journal of Medicine (2026).

articleSummary: RRTB, a new tuberculosis diagnostic method developed by Embrapa, UFJF and Fhemig, lowers cost and enables decentralization by eliminating the need for refrigerated centrifuges and biosafety cabinets. It pairs a swab sample with Löwenstein-Jensen culture, using a neutralizing acid/citrate solution to adjust pH and favor Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth, allowing small labs and rural health units to process various body fluids. In a 77-sample pilot, RRTB showed 90.91% sensitivity and 94.34% specificity versus Petroff, and 94.74% sensitivity and 92.45% specificity versus Ogawa-Kudoh, with a contamination rate of 1.30%. Validation by seven Minas Gerais reference labs with 593 sample pairs extended testing to extrapulmonary TB, zoonotic TB, and foods. The method is patented (INPI) and at TRL 8; Anvisa registration is pending for commercial scaling. It also highlights bovine TB (Mycobacterium bovis) in animals and animal-origin products, supporting One Health.

articleSummary: In Hanoi, Vietnam, a 7-day-old infant was diagnosed with Legionella pneumophila pneumonia causing respiratory distress. Long, delivered by cesarean at 39 weeks and birth weight 3.4 kg, had fever 39°C; examination noted otitis, bilateral effusions, and acute nasopharyngitis, with rapid tests for influenza A/B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 negative. Chest X-ray showed a nonuniform opacity in the right upper lung; ultrasound revealed focal consolidations in the left lung and upper right lobe with bilateral B-lines, suggesting parenchymal injury. After initial therapy, persistent fever and hypoxia required oxygen via nasal cannula. PCR on throat swab confirmed Legionella pneumophila. The infection source remained undetermined; Legionella is waterborne and linked to artificial water systems, including water for formula and humidifiers. Antibiotics were adjusted, fever resolved within 24 hours; CRP fell from 14.2 mg/dL to 1.01 mg/dL. The infant stabilized and was discharged after 7 days. Early recognition is crucial due to potential rapid deterioration.

articleHeadline: IAV develops Dengue Early Warning System to forecast dengue trends
articleSummary: Dengue Early Warning System (DEWS) developed by the Institute of Advanced Virology (IAV) in Keralam uses six years of epidemiological data (Mar 2020–Feb 2026) and meteorological data (rainfall, temperature, humidity) to generate weekly dengue forecasts. The platform integrates data from the State Surveillance Unit and the India Meteorological Department, with district-level independence to capture local geography and drainage. Predicted dengue burden is classified into four risk levels—very high, high, moderate and low—for public health planning; DEWS has shown a positive correlation with observed cases in March–July 2026 and is accessible at dews.iav.res.in. Climate factors influence transmission: warm temperatures shorten the dengue virus extrinsic incubation period, moderate-high humidity prolongs mosquito survival, and rainfall creates or flushes breeding habitats. articleHeadline: Elle convulse sans prévenir : un ver dans le cerveau et 190 œufs par gramme dans ses selles
articleSummary: An agricultural worker from the Philippines collapsed with focal seizures. MRI revealed a left frontal lobe nodular lesion with surrounding fluid, indicating neuroschistosomiasis, a rare complication of schistosomiasis caused by Schistosoma japonicum, endemic to the Philippines and also found in China and parts of Indonesia. Adult worms reside in hepatic portal vessels, but eggs migrate, causing inflammation and fibrosis that can reach the central nervous system. Diagnosis was confirmed by a 1950s serologic method in which patient serum is exposed to reference eggs, yielding a characteristic tail-like projection; stool testing counted 190 eggs per gram. The parasite’s life cycle requires freshwater contact: miracidia infect snails, which release cercariae that penetrate human skin. Treatment combined antiparasitic, anti-inflammatory, and antiepileptic therapy; after three months, seizures ceased and the MRI lesion resolved. Ongoing risk remains for rice-field workers in endemic areas.

articleHeadline: Can Vaccinating Stray Dogs Really Stop Rabies In India? Experts Explain
articleSummary: India aims to eliminate dog-mediated rabies by 2030, but controlling the source—stray dogs—remains the core challenge. Experts say ~70% vaccination coverage among dogs is needed to interrupt transmission, yet nationwide data are lacking and campaigns are uneven across states. With about 1.5 crore stray dogs in India, sustained, wide vaccination and sterilisation, plus surveillance and inter-agency coordination, are required beyond post-exposure care. After a bite, urgent wound washing with running water and soap for at least 15 minutes can reduce viral load; subsequent evaluation may include rabies vaccination (pre- or post-exposure) with a five-dose schedule on day 0, 3, 7, 14, 28, administered intramuscularly. For severe exposures, immunoglobulin may be given. The ten-day dog observation rule should not delay treatment, and vaccination should begin promptly due to rabies’ 100% fatal potential. This is the core strategy as of 2026-09-28.
